claims.explanation: Famciclovir is a prodrug of penciclovir that requires activation by viral thymidine kinase and inhibits viral DNA polymerase; human cells lack viral TK, so famciclovir's selective anticancer effects are likely due to off-target inhibition of human DNA polymerases or nucleotide metabolism, with sensitivity determined by high expression of a prodrug-activating enzyme (e.g., a nucleoside kinase) and/or loss of DNA repair, while protective features include high expression of drug efflux transporters or detoxifying enzymes.

features.basis: High deoxycytidine kinase activates nucleoside analogs; famciclovir is a nucleoside prodrug
Thymidine kinase 1 phosphorylates nucleoside analogs, potentially activating famciclovir
P-glycoprotein efflux reduces intracellular drug concentration
TP53 mutations are common in sensitive lines and may impair DNA damage response
ARID1A mutations appear in many sensitive lines and may disrupt chromatin remodeling
PTEN loss is frequent in sensitive lines and may alter survival signaling
BRAF mutations are present in several sensitive lines and may affect MAPK-driven survival
KRAS mutations are common in resistant lines and may promote survival
SMARCA4 mutation in resistant COV434 suggests chromatin remodeling loss may protect
NF1 mutations appear in resistant lines and may activate RAS signaling
ATM mutations in resistant lines may impair DNA damage response and reduce drug efficacy
POLE mutations in resistant lines may alter replication fidelity and drug response
